semantic_adjudication.reason: The PlantUML source explicitly declares three [*] --> X edges within the same region of OperationalControls (lines 26-28). UML 2.5.1 Section 14.5.6.2 specifies that an initial pseudostate has exactly one outgoing transition (or zero). Having three is a clear structural violation. The rebuttal that 'the closed model is consistent with itself' does not address the violation: the model faithfully parses the source, but the source itself declares an invalid structure. However, within the closed FCSTM as supplied, no external mechanism exists, and the NL describes behaviors that require leaving this state.
issues.title: InitialState is a reachable dead-end blocking all operational progress

issues.basis: NL3 'concurrent activation different of collision avoidance controls' while mode is active; FCSTM CollisionAvoidance has no do/entry/exit actions; three conditional initial entries at lines 38/40/42 (triggers: Start_Braking, Steering_Engaged, Alerts_Activated); verify facts initial-entry:transition:line:38/40/42 all refuted with has_trigger=true; reference inspection W_INITIAL_UNCONDITIONAL_MISSING for CollisionAvoidance (existing_conditional_count=3).
issues.expected: While CollisionAvoidance is active, the three collision avoidance controls (automatic braking, steering, alert system) are concurrently activated automatically as a do-action of the mode
issues.observed: CollisionAvoidance has no declared do-action, entry-action, or exit-action for concurrent control activation. The three region initial entries are conditional: [*]→AutomaticBraking requires /Start_Braking (line 38), [*]→SteeringControl requires /Steering_Engaged (line 40), [*]→AlertSystem requires /Alerts_Activated (line 42). Verify facts confirm all three initial entries are refuted (has_trigger=true). Controls do not auto-activate upon entering the mode; they require three separate explicit events.
issues.reason: The contract property is state_action with expected_direction=must_occur and violation_direction=missing. The NL requires concurrent activation of controls while the mode is active. The model encodes conditional region entries rather than an automatic concurrent activation action. While the regions structurally enable concurrency, the behavioral requirement of activation occurring while in the state is not satisfied by the model's transition structure. Predicate is null because the NL does not supply an exact lifecycle phase keyword (entry/do/exit) required for S4 routing.
issues.requirement_quote: The orthogonal regions of the active mode of collision avoidance allow for concurrent activation different of collision avoidance controls.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The NL says regions 'allow for' concurrent activation, which could be read as enabling (permitting) rather than requiring automatic concurrent activation. Under this reading, the conditional initial entries satisfy the requirement because they do permit concurrent activation when the three events are sent. Additionally, CollisionAvoidance is unreachable, so the action requirement is vacuously untestable in practice.
issues.title: No automatic concurrent activation action in CollisionAvoidance; region entries are conditional

decisions.basis: NL segment NL2 ('This sub-machine becomes active when a possible frontend collision, rear-end collision or collision with pedestrian is detected'), FCSTM transition:line:60 (triggers=[], guard='R45RouteToken == 15'), source transition tr_0015 (event='Collision Mode Active'), S3 predicate verdict=false, and the three detection events used on intra-composite transitions at lines 23-25.
decisions.reason: The S3 predicate confirms the transition has an empty trigger set while the NL specifies detection events as triggers for the activation. This establishes a first violated-obligation reading under the direct-trigger interpretation. However, the NL text 'becomes active when ... is detected' is naturally compatible with a causal-activation reading where the detection events trigger intra-composite transitions that eventually set the route token enabling the guarded composite-level transition. The source label 'Collision Mode Active' on the transition (tr_0015) supports the author's intent for an indirect mechanism. Both readings remain compatible with the supplied facts, constituting a surviving undercutting ambiguity.
decisions.strongest_defeater: The NL phrase 'becomes active when ... is detected' can be read as a causal/temporal requirement rather than mandating the detection events as direct triggers on this specific edge. The author's source labels the transition 'Collision Mode Active' (tr_0015), and the model uses a guard-based mechanism (R45RouteToken==15) that is set as a downstream consequence of the detection events firing on intra-composite transitions (lines 23-25). Under this reading, the detection events causally lead to activation without being the direct trigger on the activation edge itself.
decisions.violated_obligation: The activation transition from CollisionDetection to CollisionAvoidance should be triggered by at least one collision detection event (Frontend_Detected, Rear_end_Detected, or Pedestrian_Detected) per the NL requirement that the sub-machine becomes active when such a collision is detected.

decisions.basis: NL3 ('The orthogonal regions of the active mode of collision avoidance allow for concurrent activation different of collision avoidance controls'), FCSTM CollisionAvoidance with three concurrent regions each having conditional initial entries (transitions lines 38, 40, 42 with triggers Start_Braking, Steering_Engaged, Alerts_Activated respectively), verify facts confirming has_trigger=true for all three, and reference inspection W_INITIAL_UNCONDITIONAL_MISSING.
decisions.reason: The NL uses 'allow for concurrent activation' which describes structural capability rather than mandating a specific automatic activation behavior upon entry. The model's three concurrent regions with conditional initial entries do structurally allow for concurrent activation: when all three trigger events (Start_Braking, Steering_Engaged, Alerts_Activated) are received, all three regions become active simultaneously. The expected property as stated in the NL (regions allow for concurrent activation) is satisfied by the model's design. The candidate's stronger reading ('all three must enter active state simultaneously upon mode entry without external events') goes beyond what the NL text establishes.
decisions.violated_obligation: The NL states that the orthogonal regions of the active collision avoidance mode 'allow for concurrent activation of different collision avoidance controls.' The candidate reads this as requiring all three regions to enter an active state simultaneously upon mode entry, which the model does not provide (each region requires a separate trigger event).

decisions.basis: NL2 ('This sub-machine becomes active when a possible frontend collision, rear-end collision or collision with pedestrian is detected'), complete FCSTM transition inventory (26 transitions) showing PossibleCollision's outgoing edges to FrontendCollision/RearendCollision/PedestrianCollision and local exit, transition:line:60 as the sole edge to CollisionAvoidance (with guard, no trigger), and semantic binding BIND-REF003-ACTIVE-SOURCE resolving active_state to PossibleCollision.
decisions.reason: The complete transition inventory confirms no edge from PossibleCollision to CollisionAvoidance exists, establishing the first violated-obligation reading under the direct-edge interpretation. However, the NL's causal language ('becomes active when...detected') is equally compatible with the indirect activation mechanism the model provides. The binding resolves 'active_state' to PossibleCollision, but the NL does not explicitly require a direct transition FROM that state TO CollisionAvoidance - it requires that activation occurs upon detection, which the model's multi-step path achieves. Both the direct-edge reading and the causal-activation reading are competent interpretations of the NL text, and both remain compatible with the supplied model facts.
decisions.strongest_defeater: The NL text 'becomes active when ... is detected' is most naturally read as a causal/temporal requirement (CollisionAvoidance enters active state as a consequence of detection) rather than mandating a specific direct edge from PossibleCollision to CollisionAvoidance. The model provides an indirect causal mechanism: detection events trigger transitions to specific collision states (lines 23-25), which eventually lead to Collision_Mode_Active (line 26), exiting the composite, after which the guarded transition (line 60) enters CollisionAvoidance. candidate.expected: While CollisionAvoidance is active, the three collision avoidance controls (automatic braking, steering, alert system) are concurrently activated automatically as a do-action of the mode
candidate.observed: CollisionAvoidance has no declared do-action, entry-action, or exit-action for concurrent control activation. The three region initial entries are conditional: [*]→AutomaticBraking requires /Start_Braking (line 38), [*]→SteeringControl requires /Steering_Engaged (line 40), [*]→AlertSystem requires /Alerts_Activated (line 42). Verify facts confirm all three initial entries are refuted (has_trigger=true). Controls do not auto-activate upon entering the mode; they require three separate explicit events.
candidate.reason: The contract property is state_action with expected_direction=must_occur and violation_direction=missing. The NL requires concurrent activation of controls while the mode is active. The model encodes conditional region entries rather than an automatic concurrent activation action. While the regions structurally enable concurrency, the behavioral requirement of activation occurring while in the state is not satisfied by the model's transition structure. Predicate is null because the NL does not supply an exact lifecycle phase keyword (entry/do/exit) required for S4 routing.
candidate.requirement_quote: The orthogonal regions of the active mode of collision avoidance allow for concurrent activation different of collision avoidance controls.
candidate.strongest_rebuttal: The NL says regions 'allow for' concurrent activation, which could be read as enabling (permitting) rather than requiring automatic concurrent activation. Under this reading, the conditional initial entries satisfy the requirement because they do permit concurrent activation when the three events are sent. Additionally, CollisionAvoidance is unreachable, so the action requirement is vacuously untestable in practice.
candidate.title: No automatic concurrent activation action in CollisionAvoidance; region entries are conditional
